_note: v2 hooks for the abbey (B40_abbaye). Cognates use Like/plain pictures; non-cognates use gentle sound-alikes. Sacred items treated respectfully; no God the Father; no offensive shortcuts.

fr_moine_noun.hook: Like "monk", said MWAHN: a MONK in a brown habit walks the cloister garth with a wooden staff.

fr_religieux_adj.hook: Like "religious", said ruh-lee-ZHIEUH: a RELIGIOUS medal on a ribbon hangs from a cloister peg.
fr_religieux_adj.why: cognate adj; plain medal in center band

fr_abbe_noun.hook: Like "abbot", said ah-BAY: the ABBOT in a black scapular blesses the cloister with a small raised hand.

fr_vocation_noun.hook: Like "vocation", said voh-kah-SYOHN: a VOCATION pamphlet with a ringing bell sits on the cloister bench.

fr_couvent_noun.hook: Like "convent", said koo-VAHN: a miniature CONVENT with a tiny courtyard sits on the cloister ledge.

fr_monastere_noun.hook: Like "monastery", said moh-nah-STEHR: a model MONASTERY with a square cloister sits on the stone rail.

fr_abbaye_noun.hook: Like "abbey", said ah-BAY: a postcard of a famous ABBEY leans against the cloister column.

fr_religieuse_noun.hook: Like "religious" (sister), said ruh-lee-ZHIEUHZ: a nun in a simple habit waters a pot of rosemary in the garth.

fr_cloitre_noun.hook: Like "cloister", said klwah-truh: the open CLOISTER walk itself, arches and garth in plain view.
fr_cloitre_noun.why: cognate; the room is the thing

fr_novice_noun.hook: Like "novice", said noh-VEES: a young NOVICE in a white postulant's veil carries a broom along the walk.

fr_pelerinage_noun.hook: Like "pilgrimage", said peh-luh-ree-NAHZH: a PILGRIMAGE map with a shell badge lies on the cloister bench.

fr_franciscain_adj.hook: Like "Franciscan", said frahn-sees-KEN: a small brown FRANCISCAN cord with three knots lies on the credence.

fr_chartreux_adj.hook: Like "Carthusian" / Chartreux, said shar-TRUH: a silent-order CARTHUSIAN card with a mountain badge on the credence.

fr_dominicain_adj.hook: Like "Dominican", said doh-mee-nee-KEN: a black-and-white DOMINICAN shield pin rests on the credence cloth.

fr_benedictin_adj.hook: Like "Benedictine", said bay-nay-deek-TEN: a BENEDICTINE medal of St Benedict lies flat on the table.

fr_trappiste_adj.hook: Like "Trappist", said trah-PEAST: a TRAPPIST monk-profile medal hangs by a water jug — the silent order.

fr_cistercien_adj.hook: Like "Cistercian", said sees-tehr-SYEN: a plain white CISTERCIAN cowl folded on the credence.

fr_carmelite_noun.hook: Like "Carmelite", said kar-may-LEET: a CARMELITE nun in a brown habit and cream mantle holds a tiny Mount Carmel badge.

fr_moniale_noun.hook: Close to "monial" / nun, said moh-NYAL: a cloistered NUN in a black veil prays at the niche.

fr_abbesse_noun.hook: Like "abbess", said ah-BESS: the ABBESS with a small pectoral cross stands in the niche.

fr_ermite_noun.hook: Like "hermit", said ehr-MEET: a HERMIT in a rough cloak holds a simple wooden bowl.

fr_chanoine_noun.hook: Like "canon", said shah-NWAN: a CANON in choir dress holds a slim rule book.

fr_prieur_noun.hook: Like "prior", said pree-UHR: the PRIOR with a short staff of office stands by the niche.

fr_bible_noun.hook: Like "Bible", said BEEBL: a large open BIBLE on the scriptorium lectern.

fr_prophete_noun.hook: Like "prophet", said proh-FET: a scroll labeled with a PROPHET's name lies beside an inkwell.

fr_evangile_noun.hook: Like "evangel / Gospel", said ay-vahn-ZHEEL: a Gospel book with a gold cross on the cover.

fr_sermon_noun.hook: Like "sermon", said sehr-MOHN: a written SERMON sheet with a bookmark rests on the desk.

fr_apotre_noun.hook: Like "apostle", said ah-POHTR: twelve small APOTLE tokens (plain discs) in a wooden tray — one set of twelve.

fr_psaume_noun.hook: Like "psalm", said PSOHM: a PSAUM book open to a numbered psalm.

fr_breviaire_noun.hook: Like "breviary", said bray-VYAIR: a worn BREVIARY with ribbon markers.

fr_evangeliaire_noun.hook: Like "evangeliary", said ay-vahn-zhay-LYAIR: a large EVANGELIARY (Book of the Gospels) with ornate cover.

fr_psautier_noun.hook: Like "psalter", said psoh-TYAY: a PSALTER open on the copyist's desk.

fr_office_noun_m.hook: Like "office" (liturgical), said oh-FEES: an OFFICE schedule board listing the hours.

fr_amen_intj.hook: Like "amen", said ah-MEN: a carved AMEN on a choir stall end.

fr_hymne_noun_f.hook: Like "hymn", said EEM: an open HYMN book on the choir lectern.

fr_alleluia_intj.hook: Like "alleluia", said ah-lay-LUY-ah: an ALLELUIA banner hung on the choir screen.

fr_cantique_noun.hook: Like "canticle", said kahn-TEEK: a CANTICLE scroll tied with a ribbon.

fr_vigile_noun.hook: "vee-ZHEEL" ≈ vigil: a single tall VIGIL candle burns on the choir rail for the liturgical eve.

fr_vepres_noun.hook: "VEPR" ≈ viper? No — think "VESPERS": evening light fills the choir as a small clock points to sunset for VÊPRES.
fr_vepres_noun.why: vêpres=Vespers English church word; evening clock

fr_gregorien_adj.hook: Like "Gregorian", said gray-goh-RYEN: a GREGORIAN chant square-note sheet on the stand.

fr_hosanna_intj.hook: Like "hosanna", said oh-zah-NAH: a HOSANNA palm-leaf card tucked in the choir book.

fr_complies_noun.hook: "kohn-PLEE" ≈ complete: a COMPLETED daily-hours checklist is pinned up as COMPLINE closes the day.

fr_laudes_noun.hook: "LOHD" ≈ lauds / loud: a small LOUD morning hand-bell for LAUDS sits on the east choir rail.

fr_matines_noun.hook: Like "matins", said mah-TEEN: a MATINS night-office book with a moon marker rests on the stall.

fr_charite_noun.hook: Like "charity", said shah-ree-TAY: a CHARITY collection box on the refectory sideboard.

fr_aumone_noun.hook: "oh-MOHN" ≈ almond? Better: ALMS — a wooden ALMS box (aumônier style) by the refectory door.
fr_aumone_noun.why: aumône=alms English; plain alms box (meaning hook reinforced with sound oh-mohn)

fr_refectoire_noun.hook: Like "refectory", said ray-fek-TWAHR: the long REFECTORY table itself set for the meal.

fr_jeune_noun.hook: "ZHUN" ≈ June: a JUNE calendar page hangs above EMPTY plates marking the FAST (jeûne).

fr_ermitage_noun.hook: Like "hermitage", said ehr-mee-TAHZH: a tiny HERMITAGE model (quiet hut) on the shelf.

fr_benedicite_noun.hook: Like "benedicite" / grace, said bay-nay-dee-SEE-tay: a BENEDICITE grace card standing by the bread basket.
